title: EUSPA-RP-23-26 - “PRIM – Prototype for GNSS Radio-Frequency Interference Monitoring”
description: Increasing levels of GNSS radio-frequency interference (RFI) affecting satellite navigation users and infrastructures have highlighted the need for enhanced monitoring capabilities at European level. The procurement aims at concluding a direct contract for the design, development, demonstration, deployment and maintenance/support of a GNSS RFI monitoring prototype, integrating multiple data providers (open, commercial, and EU-owned) and multiple data sources (terrestrial and space) to detect GNSS RFI events and identify suspected RFI sources. The scope of the activity is limited to GNSS open-use signals. The envisaged prototype is expected to provide capabilities for: • Detection of GNSS RFI events; • Characterization and geolocation) of GNSS RFI sources; • Integration of heterogeneous terrestrial and space data sources; • Interfacing with both internal (EU-owned) and external (open, commercial, and EU-owned) data providers; • Demonstration activities and maintenance/ support during a one-year pre-operational validation phase. Where applicable, the prototype will leverage big-data analytics, machine learning, signal processing, and high-performance computing to enable real-time detection and accurate characterization of GNSS RFI events and sources. The architecture of the prototype will be designed with stringent security controls to manage information at different classification levels. This architecture will also be modular and distributed across computing nodes to enable scalability in computational capacity (data traffic, hardware resources, etc.) and coverage (geographic extent under monitoring). This prototype will support the demonstration of scalable and secure GNSS RFI monitoring and alerting while paving the way towards possible future European operational services. The contract may involve access to, handling and/or storage of classified information, which is subject to the security rules for protecting EU classified information laid down in Decision (EU, Euratom) 2015/444 and to the Decision’s implementing rules. Facility security clearance could be required as well as personnel security clearances for contractor personnel handling classified information. Special security obligations will be part of the contract (security aspects letter annexed to the contract). Subcontracting will be subject to written prior agreement by the contracting authority and compliance with all the security rules by the subcontractor and its personnel. The procurement will be subject to the eligibility and participation conditions set out in Article 24 of Regulation (EU) 2021/696 establishing the Union Space Programme.
buyer: European Union Agency for the Space Programme

title: VERIFICATION OF ADVANCED NAVIGATION ANTENNA - EXPRO+
description: Advanced satellite navigation antennas increasingly incorporate anti-jamming, anti-spoofing and adaptive beamforming capabilities to meet the growing demands of Positioning, Navigation and Timing (PNT) applications. The verification of such antennas requires realistic Over-The-Air (OTA) test environments capable of reproducing complex signal scenarios with multiple simultaneous sources arriving from different directions. Existing test approaches are often limited in their ability to reproduce realistic operational environments, leading to lengthy test campaigns and reduced capability to assess the full radiated performance of advanced navigation antennas.State-of-the-art OTA test systems based on multiple transmitting elements have demonstrated the capability to emulate representative signal environments for navigation applications. Such systems enable controlled reproduction of satellite constellations, interference sources, multipath conditions and other operational scenarios in a laboratory environment. However, current solutions oftensuffer from limited flexibility, restricted angular coverage, significant infrastructure requirements or insufficient scalability to support future generations of advanced navigation antennas.A compact, scalable and flexible OTA radiated test system based on an arrangement of transmitting elements surrounding the Antenna Under Test (AUT) needs to be developed. The developed system shall provide the capability to emulate realistic navigation signal environments, enabling repeatable laboratory verification of advanced navigation antennas and associated signal processing techniques. The system is intended to support the development and validation of future PNT technologies and shall constitute a versatile test capability for advanced navigation antenna assessment.Equipment already available at ESTEC, such as a general waveform generator (e.g. PSG) and signal analyser (e.g. PXA), and necessary for this activity will be reused for test execution.The objectives of this activity are: Develop a scalable OTA architecture based on multiple transmitting elements arranged around the Antenna Under Test. Demonstrate the capability of the system to reproduce multiple simultaneous signal sources with controlled angular distribution. Validate the performance of the developed system through representative OTA test campaigns.

title: ESA SPACE WEATHER SERVICE NETWORK PRE-OPERATION, EVOLUTIONARY MAINTENANCE AND DEVELOPMENT
description: The present activity pursues two main objectives.First, it shall ensure the continued high-quality provision of pre-operational space weather services under the existing SWE Service Network. This includes maintaining the availability of the products and servicescurrently included in the Network portfolio through the SWE Service Portal, ensuring the integration of newly developed or updated products, providing first- and second-line end-user support, delivering tailored bulletins to high-priority users, and performing continuous and evolutionary maintenance of key service components.In addition, the service catalogue shall be updated and adapted to reflect emerging and future needs of a European operational space weather service.Second, the activity shall define, design, and implement a modern Research-to-Operations-to-Research (R2O2R) framework for space weather products and services. This shall include the analysis of existing processes, the specification of the target framework, and its practical implementation within the SWE ServiceNetwork.The outcome of the activity shall enable the transition towards a new generation of the SWE Service Network and an updatedversion of the ESA SWE Service Portal.The procurement shall require the application of high standards in software engineering, theactive involvement of end-users within the R2O2R lifecycle, and the delivery of a professional, high-quality user experience for the web portal, including modern software practices, advanced graphical design, and robust human-machine interfaces.
